messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV 2 — customer 'Seraphic' (single-tenant) reporting severe tail latency / streaming stalls. Auto-alerted by QoS monitor: p99 spike above SLA threshold for last 7m. Link: https://console.redwood/example/alerts/4350001234 :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): ack. I'm on it. grabbing metrics, can someone post immediate impact? p95/p99 numbers?

maria (sre): looking — short summary from observability: last 10m: p95 ~ 300ms (ok), p99 ~ 2.1s (SLO 1.5s), streaming stall rate 14% (baseline 1.5%). Error budget alert firing.

ryan (eng-runtime): @maria thanks. Any pattern on prompt length or concurrency? single-tenant makes me suspect KV cache thrash or unusually long prefixes.

alex (oncall): @seraphic-poc can you confirm if anything changed on your side? traffic spike, new prompt templates, long prefix, or higher concurrency?

seraphic-poc: We shipped a batch job at 11:02 UTC that fanout 20k concurrent sessions for summarization. No change to prompt template besides appending a long transcript field. Some sessions are multi-k tokens.

jen (support): noted, customer confirms large prefix. tagging as possible long-prefix + high concurrency.

cory (eng-platform): I'll check recent scheduler/autoscale events. If it's sudden fanout, we might be hitting per-VM connection limits or queue pileup.

ryan (eng-runtime): If many multi-k tokens, KV cache and attention memory blowups could be causing long decode times and blocking streaming. Two quick mitigations: 1) fall back Seraphic to a smaller model variant with lower memory pressure, 2) enable conservative prefix cutoff for their tenant (truncate inputs) — both temporary. Which do we want to try first?

alex (oncall): Let's try quick options in order of least customer disruption: 1) apply prefix truncation (start with 6k -> 3k tokens), 2) if still bad, route tenant to variant-xs for new requests, 3) increase dedicated pool size (if autoscale can spin fast). I'll enact 1 now — applying tenant runtime override.

incident-bot: runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/latency-tail-live-mitigation (refer to section 'single-tenant large-prefix')

maria (sre): while alex applies truncation, I'll instrument tail heatmap for their shard. grabbing KV cache hit rate and per-req decode time histograms.

alex (oncall): applied `runtime.override.truncate_prefix_tokens=3000` for tenant seraphic-prod. Applying as dynamic policy, will affect only new requests.

ryan (eng-runtime): logs on one overloaded worker (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T11:08:12Z] tenant=seraphic request_id=aa34 decode_start latency=1.2s tokens_in_prefix=8200 kv_cache_size=1.1GB queued_wait=0.8s
[2026-03-15T11:08:13Z] tenant=seraphic request_id=aa35 decode_start latency=1.9s tokens_in_prefix=12000 kv_cache_miss=true
[2026-03-15T11:08:14Z] tenant=seraphic request_id=aa36 streaming_write_blocked=true stalled_duration=1200ms
```

jen (support): customer reports slight improvement in average latency on some requests, but streaming still stalls for long sessions.

maria (sre): KV cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 31% for seraphic's shard during the spike. Looks like cache thrash due to high variety and large prefixes. That explains p99 jumps and streaming stalls.

cory (eng-platform): Autoscale cannot spin up enough specialized instances quickly due to cold-start image pull  — we can temporarily increase burst capacity by enabling reserved fallback nodes (we have 4 warm nodes). Alex, want me to route their traffic to warm pool?

alex (oncall): Yes, route seraphic to warm nodes for next 20m. Also enable reduce-concurrency-per-worker for this tenant to alleviate KV pressure: set `tenant.max_concurrency_per_worker=2`.

ryan (eng-runtime): Planning a longer-term mitigation: implement per-tenant prefix-length-aware caching and evictions; but that's a code change. For now, two short-term patches: 1) prefix truncation (done), 2) route to smaller model variant for new sessions (variant-xs uses less KV and shorter decode times). Recommend coordinated rollback if customer needs full fidelity.

alex (oncall): implementing routing to variant-xs for new sessions now. Notifying customer this will reduce fidelity for extremely long contexts.

seraphic-poc: fine to use truncated context for now, we need service stable. We'll evaluate after spike.

incident-bot: NOTE: SLO breach window currently active. Incident severity remains SEV 2. Please update incident ticket after mitigations: https://tickets.redwood/INC-8792

maria (sre): Post-mitigation metrics (5m after changes): p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 1.1s, streaming stall rate down to 3.2% — still above baseline but under breach threshold. Good progress.

alex (oncall): marking this thread for handoff to eng-runtime for RCA and longer-term fix. @ryan you'll take lead? Also @cory to track autoscale/warm-pool improvements.

ryan (eng-runtime): I'll own RCA. Immediate action items: - collect sample traces for top 50 p99 requests - reproduce locally with a few long prefixes - prototype per-tenant cache eviction heuristics. I'll open a PR tracker and link to INC-8792.

cory (eng-platform): I'll write a postmortem action to reduce cold-start time and add more warm nodes for dedicated single-tenant pools.

jen (support): I'll send a customer note summarizing actions taken and estimated ETA for full recovery (24-48h for deeper changes).

alex (oncall): handoff: I'm stepping off on-call in 40m. Handoff notes: mitigations applied (prefix truncation, route to variant-xs, route to warm pool, concurrency limit); monitoring in place; SRE/Runtime owning follow-up. If we see another breach, escalate to SEV1.

ryan (eng-runtime): got it. I'll coordinate follow-ups and post an RCA draft in the incident ticket by EOD.

maria (sre): adding final: probable root cause = single-tenant large-prefix fanout causing KV cache thrash + autoscale cold-start delays -> streaming stalls and p99 tail spikes. Action items logged.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation applied, ongoing monitoring. Assigned owners: ryan (eng-runtime), cory (eng-platform), maria (sre), jen (support). Update INC-8792 when RCA ready. :white_check_mark:
